chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was leaning upon me, or he said, upon my father, so Abbad ibn Kathir al-Basri came upon him, and upon him were Mervian clothes that were beautiful. He said, 'O Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)! You are from the People of the Household of the Prophethood, and your father was [such and such], so what are these Mervian clothes upon you? If only you would wear [something] besides these clothes.'

So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him, 'Woe be unto you, O Abbad! Who has prohibited the adornment of Allah which He brought forth for His servants, and the good provisions? Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, when He bestows a favor upon His servant, loves that He sees it upon him. There is no problem with it. Woe be unto you, O Abbad! I am but a part of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so do not hurt me.'
And it was so that Abbad wore two Qatary clothes.

key_terms.ثِيَابٌ مَرْوِيَّةٌ: Clothes from Merv, known for their quality and luxury
key_terms.قِطْرِيَّيْنِ: Two clothes from Qatara, a type of fabric

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on wearing fine and luxurious clothing for men according to the Ahl al-Bayt?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia jurisprudential principle of 'takhalluq' (adornment) by validating the use of high-quality fabrics like Mervian silk for the Ahl al-Bayt, countering the notion that asceticism requires rejecting luxury. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) grounds his response in the Quranic concept that divine favor is best appreciated when visibly manifested, thereby establishing a theological basis for dignified appearance as an act of gratitude. The narrative also subtly reinforces the Imam's unique status as 'badr' (part) of the Prophet, suggesting that their adornment carries a distinct spiritual weight compared to general believers.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qadah who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> was leaning upon me’, or said, ‘Upon my father’, so Abbad Bin Kaseer Al Basry came over and upon him<sup>asws</sup> were clothes of Merv (a city), so he said, ‘O Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>! You<sup>asws</sup> are from the People<sup>asws</sup> of the Household of the Prophet-hood, and your<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> was what he<sup>asws</sup> was, so what are these Mervian clothes upon you<sup>asws</sup>? If only you<sup>asws</sup> would wear besides these clothes’.

So Abu Abdullahasws said to him: ‘Woe be unto you, O Abbad! [7:32] Say: Who has prohibited the adornments of Allah which He has Brought forth for His servants and the good provisions? When Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Favours upon Hisazwj servant with a Bounty Loves that Heazwj Sees it upon him. There is no problem with it. Woe be unto you, O Abbad! But rather, Iasws am a part of Rasool-Allahsaww, therefore do not hurt measws’.
And it was so that Abbad had worn two Qatary (a city) clothes’.
en.sarwar: 13. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad al-Astdariy from ibn al-Qaddah who has said the following:

“Once abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was leaning against me or he said, ‘against my father’ when ‘Abbad ibn Kathir al-Basriy met him (the Imam) and he (the Imam) had a dress of fabrics made in Marw (name of place) of fine quality. He (‘Abbad) said, ‘O abu ‘Abd Allah, you are of the family of the Holy Prophet, and your father was (so pious). What is this dress, made in Marw, on you? I wish you dressed in a lower quality dress.’

Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said to him, ‘Woe on you, O ‘Abbad! Who has made unlawful the beautiful things that Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has brought out for His servants and the very fine kinds of means of sustenance. When Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, grants bounties on His servant He loves to see it on him and it is not harmful. Woe on you, O ‘Abbad, I am a piece of the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, do not trouble me.’
‘Abbad wore two pieces of clothes made in Qitr (name of a place).”’
